title: Coroutine Exception Handling
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of coroutine exception handling using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates coroutine exception handling.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Coroutine Exception Handling** as part of **Coroutines, Asynchronous Programming, and Concurrency**. Catch or represent expected failures at a boundary where the program can respond usefully; do not silently swallow errors or expose secrets in messages. Use the subtopics—Propagating Exceptions, Supervisor Jobs, Coroutine Exception Handlers—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Asynchronous code introduces lifecycle, cancellation, and shared-state concerns. Structured concurrency and explicit data flow make these concerns easier to reason about.

items.title: Coroutine Exception Handlers
items.text: Coroutine Exception Handlers depends on task lifetime and execution context. Keep child tasks inside an owning scope, handle cancellation cooperatively, and avoid unsynchronized shared mutable state.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: A suspend function always runs on a background thread automatically.
